rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Both readings, shiqwatuna and shaqawatuna, are sound; the former is a verbal noun like raqqah and fitnah, while the latter parallels saʿādah.
rows.anchor: الشقوة مصدر كالرقة والفطنة والشقاوة كالسعادة فالقراءة بهما جميعا سائغة

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Sukhriyyan and sukhriyyan can describe mocking someone; Abu Ubayda distinguishes mocking them from making them serve, while Hasan and Qatada distinguish service with ḍamma from mockery with kasra.
rows.anchor: وحكي عن الحسن وقتادة أن ما كان من العبودة فهو سخري بالضم وما كان من الهزء فبالكسر

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Kasra is more common for mockery; he explains the forms through the verbal noun sukhriy and the difference in the nisba endings, while Yunus allows the ḍamma form for mockery too.
rows.anchor: الأكثر في الهزء كسر السين فيما حكوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lafḥ and nafḥ both mean a scorching touch, but lafḥ has a stronger and more severe effect on the face.
rows.anchor: اللفح والنفح بمعنى إلا أن اللفح أشد تأثيرا وأعظم من النفح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kuluḥ is the lips drawing back from the teeth until the teeth show; al-Aʿshā’s verse illustrates the word kalih.
rows.anchor: والكلوح تقلص الشفتين عن الأسنان حتى تبدو الأسنان قال الأعشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhsaʾa means to rebuke someone so they retreat; the command also implies retreating in a degraded state.
rows.anchor: ومعنى أخسأ أي تباعد تباعد منحط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the clause beginning idhā nufikha, the governing element is the phrase baynahum; yawmaʾidhin is the predicate of an elided lā, understood as no kinship remains among them.
rows.anchor: العامل في إذا نفخ وبينهم ويومئذ خبر لا المحذوف تقديره فلا أنساب تثبت بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talfaḥu wujūhahum is an accusative circumstantial clause, with khālidūn as its governor.
rows.anchor: تلفح وجوههم النار في موضع النصب على الحال والعامل فيه خالدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An implied verb is needed for the interpretation that people will neither boast by lineage nor show kinship based compassion.
rows.anchor: ولا بد من تقدير محذوف في الآية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Jubbāʾī say the verse denies boasting about lineage; people will be distinguished by deeds, not ancestry.
rows.anchor: لا يتفاخرون بالأنساب كما كانوا يفعلونه في الدنيا عن ابن عباس والجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Either interpretation requires an understood verb: they will not boast by lineage or show kinship-based compassion, and no one will outrank another by ancestry.
rows.anchor: وإنما يتفاضلون بأعمالهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says every lineage and noble descent is severed on Judgment Day except the Prophet’s own lineage and kinship.
rows.anchor: كل حسب ونسب منقطع يوم القيامة إلا حسبي ونسبي

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: They do not ask about one another’s condition as they did in worldly life, since each is preoccupied with himself.
rows.anchor: لا يسأل بعضهم بعضا عن حاله وخبره كما كانوا يسألون في الدنيا لشغل كل واحد بنفسه عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that they do not ask others to carry their sins for them.
rows.anchor: لا يسأل بعضهم بعضا أن يحمل عنه ذنبه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: There is no conflict with people questioning one another elsewhere: the Resurrection has different stages, some so terrifying that no one asks, and others when they do.
rows.anchor: هذه تارات يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: A further view places the questioning among the people of Paradise as they enter it, after they are safe from the terrors of Judgment.
rows.anchor: إنما يتساءلون عند دخول الجنة وإنما يسأل بعض أهل الجنة بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whose scales are heavy through acts of obedience are the successful ones who are saved.
rows.anchor: بالطاعات { فأولئك هم المفلحون } الناجون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whose scales are light because of deficient obedience have lost themselves and remain in Hell; the mechanics of weighing were discussed under al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: عن الطاعات { فأولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire’s flames strike their faces; kalih describes a grimacing expression, and Ibn Abbas glosses it as frowning.
rows.anchor: أي يصيب وجوههم لفح النار ولهبها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan describes the damned as lips contracted until their teeth show, like roasted heads.
rows.anchor: هو أن تتقلص شفاههم وتبدو أسنانهم كالرؤوس المشوية عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke asks whether the Quran, or God’s proofs and arguments, had not been recited to them in worldly life.
rows.anchor: ألم تكن حججي وبيناتي وأدلتي تقرأ عليكم في دار الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their shiqwah is the harm that overtakes well-being; the evil deeds that caused their misery overcame them, and neglecting God for idols and desire is the gravest misery.
rows.anchor: استعلت علينا سيئاتنا التي أوجبت لنا الشقاء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The condemned ask to be returned from the Fire so they can abandon disbelief, denial, and sin; Hasan says this is the last speech they make before groaning like donkeys.
rows.anchor: هذا آخر كلام يتكلم به أهل النار ثم بعد ذلك يكون لهم شهيق كشهيق الحمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akhsaʾū is a rebuke used to drive away dogs; addressed to people, it humiliates them with the degradation their punishment deserves.
rows.anchor: وهذه اللفظة زجر للكلاب وإذا قيل ذلك للإنسان يكون للإهانة المستحقة للعقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order not to speak either intensifies humiliation and anger or specifically means they may not ask for relief; it is not a literal legal prohibition, since obligation and prohibition no longer apply in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وهي على صيغة النهي وليست بنهي لأن الأمر والنهي مرتفعان في الآخرة لارتفاع التكليف

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and others say prayer belongs to humans while every other creature glorifies God.
rows.anchor: إن الصلاة للإنسان والتسبيح لكل شيء عن مجاهد وجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best reading is that God knows the worship of all creatures, because only God knows how everything signifies Him.
rows.anchor: وهو أجود لأن الأشياء كلها لا يعلم كيفية دلالتها على الله وإنما يعلم الله تعالى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what creatures do and recompenses them accordingly; His is the full dominion and governance of the heavens and earth, and all return to Him at resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي عالم بأفعالهم فيجازيهم بحسبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gently drives clouds, joins their scattered portions, piles them up, and rain emerges through their openings.
rows.anchor: أي يسوقه سوقا رفيقا إلى حيث يريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains of hail may be mountains within the clouds, where hail gathers before falling; al-Balkhī and others hold this view.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون البرد يجتمع في السحاب كالجبال ثم ينزل عنها عن البلخي

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ interprets the phrase as a quantity of hail as great as mountains, like saying one has two housefuls of straw.
rows.anchor: معناه وينزل من السماء مقدار جبال من برد كما يقول عندي بيتان من تبن أي قدر بيتين عن الفراء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan and al-Jubbāʾī take the verse literally as referring to created mountains of hail in the familiar heaven.
rows.anchor: أراد السماء المعروفة فيها جبال من برد مخلوقة عن الحسن والجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hail can destroy crops and property, while God’s withholding it from others is a mercy; sending it is punishment and withholding its harm is blessing.
rows.anchor: أي ويصرف ضرره عمن يشاء فيكون إصابته نقمة وصرفه نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cloud’s lightning nearly blinds people because of its intense flash, as in the comparison with lightning snatching sight.
rows.anchor: يقرب ضوء برق السحاب من أن يذهب بالبصر ويخطفه لشدة لمعانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alternates night and day, making one follow the other and merging one into the other as a lesson for people of insight.
rows.anchor: يصرفهما في اختلافهما وتعاقبهما وإدخال أحدهما في الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every animal that moves on earth was created from water, understood either as semen or as the primordial element from which animal life derives; jinn and angels are excluded from the first sense.
rows.anchor: كل حيوان يدب على وجه الأرض ولا يدخل فيه الجن والملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reciters read sirājan, while the Kufans other than ʿĀṣim read surujan; the singular reading is supported by the verse calling the sun a lamp, while the plural evokes the stars as lamps.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سراجا فحجته قوله وجعل فيها سراجا ومن قرأ سرجا فحجته قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading yadhakkara is light for Hamza and Khalaf and doubled for the remaining readers; the text says its argument was given earlier.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة وخلف أن يذكر خفيفا والباقون يذكر بتشديدتين

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The readings of yaqturū and yuqtirū have related forms; with ḍamma the meaning is not to be miserly, and with fatḥa it means not to restrict spending.
rows.anchor: فمن ضم الياء أراد لم يقتروا في إنفاقهم لأن المسرف مشرف على الإقتار ومن فتح الياء فالمعنى لم يضيقوا في الإنفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Several readers make yudaʿʿaf and yukhlad jussive, others raise them, and Abu Bakr reads yuḍāʿaf with alif; Ḥafṣ lengthens the kasra in fīhi.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر ويعقوب وسهل يضعف له العذاب بالتشديد والجزم ويخلد بالجزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Barjamī reports a variant with a still bāʾ in yubaddil; the other readers use the doubled form.
rows.anchor: قرأ يبدل الله بسكون الباء البرجمي عن أبي بكر مختلفا عنه والباقون بالتشديد

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The verb qatar has both ḍamma and fatḥa patterns, like ʿakafa and ʿarasha, and the readings express the idea of moderate spending rather than extravagance or stinginess.
rows.anchor: وأما قتر يقتر ويقتر فمثل عكف يعكف ويعكف وعرش يعرش ويعرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet’s aqtara is used of the poor man, by ellipsis for a man who has become impoverished; the same adjective-for-noun construction occurs in the Quran.
rows.anchor: فأقام الصفة مقام الموصوف ومثله في التنزيل

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali compares the omitted complement in yalqa athāman with an omitted genitive understood as the recompense of sins, and cites Quranic parallels.
rows.anchor: في قوله يلق أثاما أي جزاء أثام

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: In yalqa athāman, the omitted complement is understood as the recompense for sin, as in the Quranic example about the wrongdoers being apprehensive of what they earned.
rows.anchor: ومثل حذف الجزاء الذي هو مضاف في المعنى في قوله يلق أثاما

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses athām as punishment and cites a verse about punishment being the consequence of disobedience.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيدة: يلق أثاما أي عقوبة وأنشد لمسافع الليثي

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali also relates athām to a line by Bishr, while the raised forms of yuḍāʿaf and yukhlad begin a new clause rather than continuing the preceding condition.
rows.anchor: ومن رفع يضاعف ويخلد قطعه عما قبله واستأنف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yudaʿʿaf and yuḍāʿaf have the same sense, as do yubaddal and yubaddil.
rows.anchor: وأما يضاعف ويضعف فهما في المعنى سواء وكذلك يبدل ويبدل

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Khilfah means that each thing follows another: night succeeds day, and day succeeds night; Zuhayr’s verse witnesses this sense.
rows.anchor: الخلفة كل شيء بعد شيء الليل خلفه النهار والنهار خلفه الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hawn is the verbal noun of hayyin and denotes calmness and dignified bearing.
rows.anchor: والهون مصدر الهين في السكينة والوقار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gharām is the most severe, persistent torment; the word is linked to a creditor who stays with someone, and to being constantly attached to women.
rows.anchor: والغرام أشد العذاب وهو اللازم الملح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who walk humbly is the predicate of servants of the Merciful, or a descriptive clause; hawn is circumstantial, salāman is an elided verbal noun, and mustaqarran/maqāman are specifications.
rows.anchor: الذين يمشون خبر المبتدأ الذي هو عباد الرحمن ويجوز أن يكون خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their spending is balanced between extravagance and miserliness; bayna dhālika can explain qawāman or attach to kāna or its predicate.
rows.anchor: وكان بين ذلك قواما أي كان الإنفاق ذا قوام بين الإسراف والإقتار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven wandering celestial bodies move through twelve named zodiac stations; another view from Hasan, Mujahid, and Qatada says burūj are the great visible stars.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هي النجوم الكبار عن الحسن ومجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular sirāj means the sun; the plural reading can mean the sun together with the planets, while the moon shines when the sun is absent.
rows.anchor: يعني الشمس ومن قرأ سرجا أراد الشمس والكواكب معها

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Khilfah means each period succeeds the other, allowing someone who missed a night act to make it up by day and vice versa; this explanation is reported from Umar, Ibn Abbas, and Hasan.
rows.anchor: فمن فاته عمل الليل استدركه بالنهار ومن فاته عمل النهار استدركه بالليل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from Abu Abd Allah says to make up daytime prayer at night and nighttime prayer during the day.
rows.anchor: تقضي صلاة النهار بالليل وصلاة الليل بالنهار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid instead explains night and day as opposites, one black and the other white.
rows.anchor: معناه أنه جعل كل واحد منهما مخالفا لصاحبه فجعل أحدهما أسود والآخر أبيض عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering means reflecting that a manager and controller unlike either night or day must exist, and turning worship to Him; gratitude can mean thanking God for His blessings in both periods.
rows.anchor: يتفكر ويستدل بذلك على أن لهما مدبرا ومصرفا لا يشبههما ولا يشبهانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first interpretation, gratitude refers to voluntary worship after completing the obligatory prayer.
rows.anchor: وعلى القول الأول فمعناه أو أراد النافلة بعد أداء الفريضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cited verse, the question about seeing a wolf is a rhetorical description of ḍayḥ; ḍayḥ is milk mixed with water, with a greenish or gray cast.
rows.anchor: فقوله: هل رأيت الذئب قط جملة استفهامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Winds bearing rain announce good news; God sends them in varying directions, including north, south, ṣabā, and dabūr, according to the benefit He knows.
rows.anchor: وإرسال الرياح تحريكها وإجراؤها في الجهات المختلفة تارة شمالا وتارة جنوبا صبا وأخرى دبورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mercy tasted is rain, which also enables ships to sail by God’s command; another view takes seeking bounty as cultivating through rainfall.
rows.anchor: لتطلبوا بالأمطار فيما تزرعونه من فضل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase laʿallakum tashkurūn gently urges gratitude, just as the Quran gently invites generosity with the question who will lend God a good loan.
rows.anchor: تلطف سبحانه بلفظ لعلكم في الدعاء إلى الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier messengers brought clear miracles and signs, were rejected, and God punished the guilty; His promise to aid believers means defending them with proof and repelling their enemies.
rows.anchor: وكان حقا علينا نصر المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Ibn Abbas via Abu Amr read the passive yusmaʿ al-ṣumm, while other readers use the active tusmiʿ al-ṣumm; the reading was discussed under al-Naml.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وابن عباس عن أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim and Hamza read ḍuʿfin with ḍamma, while the other readers use fatḥa; the reading was discussed under al-Anfāl.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم وحمزة من ضعف بالضم والباقون بفتح الضاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional clause’s answer is omitted because the oath’s answer, la-ẓallū, supplies it; the lām is called a preparatory oath-lām by Basrans and a warning oath-lām by Kufans.
rows.anchor: قد حذف لأنه قد أغنى عنه جواب القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destructive wind yellows either the crop that had been green and fresh or, in another view, the clouds because yellow clouds carry no rain.
rows.anchor: إن الهاء يعود إلى السحاب ومعناه: فرأوا السحاب مصفرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After once hoping and rejoicing, people turn ungrateful; this is the behavior of one who ignores the wise Creator, who should be thanked in ease and obeyed in hardship.
rows.anchor: فيشكر عند النعمة ويصبر عند الشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers are likened to the dead and the deaf because they do not benefit from the Prophet’s call; their turning away is refusal of the evidence and a path of error.
rows.anchor: تارة بالأموات وتارة بالصم لأنهم لا ينتفعون بدعاء الداعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind cannot be guided from their error when they do not seek insight; only those who believe in God’s signs benefit from the Prophet’s call and submit.
rows.anchor: ليس تسمع إلا من يصدق بآياتنا وأدلتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates people from weakness, either as drops of semen or as helpless infants, gives them youthful strength, then weakness and gray hair in old age.
rows.anchor: معناه خلقكم أطفالا لا تقدرون على البطش

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: The criminals swear at resurrection that they remained in their graves for only an hour; this interpretation is attributed to al-Kalbi and Muqatil.
rows.anchor: غير ساعة } واحدة عن الكلبي ومقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals may mean they spent only an hour in worldly life because they regard its duration as insignificant, or only an hour after the punishment of the grave ceased; al-Jubbāʾī and Matta hold the latter.
rows.anchor: يحلفون ما مكثوا في الدنيا غير ساعة لاستقلالهم مدة الدنيا

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: To explain false oaths despite certain knowledge in the afterlife, Abu Ali and Abu Hashim say they swear according to their conjecture, since they did not know how long they remained in the graves.
rows.anchor: أنهم حلفوا على الظن ولم يعلموا لبثهم في القبور

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن الإخشيد
rows.claim: Another answer is that their oaths could occur before their minds were fully developed.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك يجوز أن يقع منهم قبل إكمال عقولهم عن أبي بكر بن الإخشيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects using this verse to deny punishment in the grave, since they may mean that only an hour passed after God’s punishment there.
rows.anchor: ومن استدل في هذه الآية على نفي عذاب القبر فقد أبعد لما بينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuʾfakūn can mean that they lied in worldly life or that ignorance turned them away from truth in both abodes.
rows.anchor: يصرفون صرفهم جهلهم عن الحق في الدارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Amr and Khalaf alone read the passive yujzā kullu kafūr; other readers use active najzī with kull as its object.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمر وخلف وحده يجزي كل كفور على ما لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some readers use singular bayyinah and others plural bayyināt: singular can mean the scripture or what the Prophet brought, while plural reflects each prophet’s proof or the scripture’s several kinds of evidence.
rows.anchor: الوجه في قراءة بينة على الإفراد أنه يجعل ما في الكتاب أو ما يأتي به النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iṣṭirākh is a cry for help, formed from iṣ-ṣurākh with tāʾ changed into ṭāʾ to match the emphatic ṣād while retaining a similar articulation point.
rows.anchor: الاصطراخ الصياح والنداء بالاستغاثة افتعال من الصراخ قلبت التاء طاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqt means hatred; maqtahu means he hated him, and the person hated is mamqūt or maqīt.
rows.anchor: والمقت البغض مقته يمقته وهو ممقوت ومقيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers do not die and find relief, nor is the Fire’s punishment eased; this is how every persistent denier of God and His prophets is requited.
rows.anchor: بالموت { فيموتوا } فيستريحوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plea to return means they promise faith and obedience instead of disbelief and sin, but God rebukes them for having had enough time to reflect and learn.
rows.anchor: ردنا إلى الدنيا لنعمل بالطاعات التي تأمرنا بها

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
rows.claim: One report says the age that removes any excuse is sixty years; this is also one report from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: العمر الذي أعذر الله فيه إلى ابن آدم ستون سنة وهو إحدى الروايتين عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says that whoever is granted sixty years has received sufficient time and has no excuse.
rows.anchor: من عمره الله ستين سنة فقد أعذر إليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Other views identify the adequate age as forty years, or as a rebuke specifically directed to an eighteen-year-old; the latter is reported from Wahb, Qatada, and al-Sadiq.
rows.anchor: هو أربعون سنة عن ابن عباس ومسروق

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: The warner is Muhammad, according to Ibn Zayd, al-Jubbāʾī, and others; alternatives identify him as the Quran, gray hair, deaths of relatives, or full maturity of reason.
rows.anchor: أي المخوف من عذاب الله وهو محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Ali identifies the warner as the Quran; Ikrima and Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna identify it as gray hair and cite poetry to support that usage.
rows.anchor: النذير القرآن عن زيد بن علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned are told to taste their punishment and remorse, for no helper can repel it from wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: أي فذوقوا العذاب وحسرة الندم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: God made the disbelievers successors, one community after another; another view says they inherited the earth after earlier generations.
rows.anchor: جعلكم معاشر الكفار أمة بعد أمة وقرنا بعد قرن عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The harm and punishment of disbelief fall on the disbeliever, and disbelief increases God’s aversion toward them and their loss and destruction.
rows.anchor: { ولا يزيد الكافرين كفرهم إلا خسارا } أي خسرانا وهلاكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural makānāt is read by Abu Bakr alone; other readers use the singular, and the text refers readers to an earlier discussion.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو بكر وحده مكاناتهم على الجمع والباقون على التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reciters pronounce nunakkis-hu with a doubled, kasra-marked kāf, while others use the lighter form; doubling can indicate repetition or intensity.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة وسهل ننكسه بضم النون الأولى وفتح الثانية وكسر الكاف وتشديدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some read tunḏira as a direct address to the Prophet; others use yunḏira for the Quran or for God.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ لتنذر بالتاء فهو خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن قرأ بالياء أراد القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭams is erasing something until no trace remains; on the eye it removes the opening between the eyelids, and mask is transformation into a deformed shape.
rows.anchor: الطمس محو الشيء حتى يذهب أثره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God could blind the disbelievers so they lose guidance; Hasan, Qatada, and al-Jubbāʾī say they would be left blind and wandering.
rows.anchor: لتركناهم عميا يترددون عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blinded people might seek the path of truth, salvation, or simply the roads to their homes, but could not see their way.
rows.anchor: فطلبوا طريق الحق وقد عموا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could instead transform them into apes and swine where they sit, or into stones without souls; they then could neither go nor return, whether from place or from the punishment and transformed state.
rows.anchor: لعذبناهم بنوع آخر من العذاب فأقعدناهم في منازلهم ممسوخين قردة وخنازير

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Growing very old reverses a person’s bodily development: strength, size, freshness, and knowledge decline toward a condition like childhood.
rows.anchor: ونرده إلى حال الهرم التي تشبه حال الصبي في ضعف القوة وعزوب العلم عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The decline of old age should make people reason that the one who made them this way can also bring them back to life.
rows.anchor: أفلا تتدبرون في أن الله تعالى يقدر على الإعادة كما قدر على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not teach Muhammad the craft or composition of poetry, and poetry was not fitting for him.
rows.anchor: يعني قول الشعراء وصناعة الشعر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan relates that the Prophet recited a line in altered order; Abu Bakr corrected it, and the incident demonstrated that the Prophet had not been taught poetry.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يتمثل بهذا البيت

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports another occasion when the Prophet reshaped a line; Abu Bakr corrected him, and the Prophet said he was not a poet and poetry was not fitting for him.
rows.anchor: ليس هكذا يا رسول الله فيقول: إني لست بشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase I am the Prophet without a lie, son of Abd al-Muttalib was either not poetry or an accidental utterance rather than intentional composition.
rows.anchor: فقد قال قوم: إن هذا ليس بشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the Quran was not taught as poetry and its composition is not poetic; the Prophet did hear poetry and encouraged it.
rows.anchor: وما علمناه الشعر بتعليم القرآن وما ينبغى للقرآن أن يكون شعرا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told Hassan ibn Thabit that he would remain supported by the Holy Spirit while defending the community with his tongue.
rows.anchor: لا تزال يا حسان مؤيدا بروح القدس ما نصرتنا بلسانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God wanted a child as pagans, Christians, or Jews claim, He would choose whom He wished from creation, not leave the choice to them; the claim is impossible and is rejected.
rows.anchor: على ما يقوله هؤلاء من أن الملائكة بنات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted above taking a child: He is one, without partner or spouse, and overcomes creation through death while remaining deathless.
rows.anchor: لخلقه بالموت وهو حي لا يموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth were created for a wise purpose, not in vain; day and night progressively cover one another through increase and decrease, according to Hasan and other commentators.
rows.anchor: يدخل كل واحد منهما على صاحبه بالزيادة والنقصان فما يزيد في أحدهما ينقص من الآخر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets the alternation as covering one another or one entering the other, citing Quranic parallels.
rows.anchor: يغشي هذا كما قال يغشي الليل النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon follow a regular course to an appointed limit, which may mean the end God set for them, the Resurrection, or a known seasonal rising and setting time.
rows.anchor: أي إلى مدة قدرها الله لهما أن يجريا إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one capable of creating and governing the heavens, earth, sun, and moon is not in need of a child or partner; the verse demonstrates His power and freedom from need.
rows.anchor: فهو منزه عن اتخاذ الولد والشريك فإن ذلك من صفة المحتاجين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The manifest loss is obvious and cannot be hidden; the phrase echoes the description of inheritors of Paradise.
rows.anchor: أي البين الظاهر الذي لا يخفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Layers and canopies of fire and smoke surround the damned above and below; the lower coverings may be the couches of fire, since Hell has levels, or a metaphor for fire enclosing every side.
rows.anchor: إنما سمي ما تحتهم من النار ظللا لأنها ظلل لمن تحتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ẓulal may be applied expansively to pieces of fire because they correspond to the shade promised to the people of Paradise.
rows.anchor: أجرى اسم الظلل على قطع النار على سبيل التوسع والمجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God describes this punishment to frighten His servants as an act of mercy, so they will avoid it by obeying His commands; the following imperative completes the warning.
rows.anchor: ذلك الذي وصف من العذاب يخوف الله به عباده ورحمة لهم ليتقوا عذابه بامتثال أوامره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The yāʾ is omitted from the two occurrences of yā ʿibād because the preceding kasra indicates it.
rows.anchor: وإنما حذف الياء في الموضعين لأن الكسرة تدل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ on whether the subject of the verb about excuses is feminine or masculine; both forms are good because maʿdhirah and iʿtidhār have the same sense.
rows.anchor: والوجهان حسنان لأن المعذرة والاعتذار بمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase yawm yaqūm al-ashhād is grammatically attached to the earlier reference to worldly life.
rows.anchor: محمول على موضع قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God aids messengers and believers in worldly life through proof, victory in battle, divine support and strengthened resolve, destroying enemies, saving believers, or avenging them; the form of aid follows wisdom.
rows.anchor: فإن النصر قد يكون بالحجة ويكون أيضا بالغلبة في المحاربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One example of divine vengeance for a prophet is the report that seventy thousand people were killed in retaliation when Yahya son of Zakariya was killed.
rows.anchor: كما نصر يحيى بن زكريا لما قتل حين قتل به سبعون ألفا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The witnesses on Judgment Day may be angels, prophets, and believers, according to Qatada; Mujahid identifies them as guardian angels, while another view says only prophets.
rows.anchor: هم الملائكة والأنبياء والمؤمنون عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoers’ excuses and repentance will not help in the afterlife, because compelled action there is not praiseworthy; they face exclusion from mercy and Hell.
rows.anchor: لأن الآخرة دار الإلجاء إلى العمل والملجأ غير محمود على العمل الذي ألجىء إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Moses the Torah containing clear proofs of divine unity and passed it to the Israelites as guidance and reminder for people of understanding.
rows.anchor: أي أعطيناه التوراة فيها أدلة واضحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is commanded to endure his people’s abuse because God’s promise of victory in this life and reward in the next is true; the reading treats seeking forgiveness as a command for a minor sin only if such sins are possible for prophets.
rows.anchor: يا محمد على أذى قومك وتحمل المشاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound view is that seeking forgiveness is devotional: it raises the Prophet’s rank and establishes a practice for later believers, rather than implying a sin by him.
rows.anchor: هذا تعبد من الله سبحانه لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glorifying God with praise means declaring Him transcendent, thanking Him, attributing blessings to Him, and denying any likeness; another view purifies His attributes or deeds from created or unjust qualities.
rows.anchor: نزه الله تعالى واعترف بشكره وإضافة النعم إليه ونفي التشبيه عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the command to glorify God as a command to pray.
rows.anchor: معناه صل بأمر ربك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: For Mujahid, al-ʿashī extends from the sun’s decline until night and al-ibkār from the second dawn until sunrise; Ibn Abbas instead identifies the five prayers.
rows.anchor: من طلوع الفجر الثاني إلى طلوع الشمس عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report quotes God telling people to remember Him for an hour after morning and after afternoon, promising to take care of their concerns.
rows.anchor: يا بن آدم اذكرني بعد الغداة ساعة وبعد العصر ساعة أكفك ما أهمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are urged to answer their Lord’s call through Muhammad and submit to obedience before a day that cannot be returned from; the day may be Judgment, which no one can repel, or death, which cannot be delayed.
rows.anchor: أجيبوا داعي ربكم يعني محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما دعاكم إليه

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī identifies the day as Judgment, after which no one can return to the world and which no one can repel.
rows.anchor: لا يقدر أحد على رده ودفعه وهو يوم القيامة عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim identifies the day as death, which cannot be turned aside or postponed from its appointed time.
rows.anchor: لا يرد ولا يؤخر عن وقته وهو يوم الموت عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day there is no refuge from punishment and no way to deny or alter it; another explanation of nakīr is a helper who would deny what befalls them.
rows.anchor: أي معقل يعصمكم من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the unbelievers turn away, the Prophet is not charged with guarding them from disobedience; his only duty is clear delivery of the message and explanation of guidance.
rows.anchor: إلى أفهامهم والبيان لما فيه رشدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a person receives mercy and rejoices, the blameworthy joy is accompanied by arrogance, denial, or ingratitude; mercy may specifically mean health.
rows.anchor: أي بطر لأن الفرح المراد هنا ما قارنه أشر أو جحودا أو إنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When misfortune strikes because of their deeds, people enumerate their calamities and deny God’s blessings; hardship can be drought, poverty, illness, or other distress.
rows.anchor: الإنسان كفور } يعدد المصيبة ويجحد النعم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: The phrase about granting both sons and daughters means a woman bears a boy, then a girl, and repeats this sequence, according to Mujahid.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: هو أن تلد المرأة غلاما ثم جارية

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd explains the phrase as bearing twins: either a boy and a girl, two boys, or two girls; Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya says a womb combines male and female.
rows.anchor: أن تلد توأما ذكرا وأنثى أو ذكرا ذكرا أو أنثى أنثى عن ابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s dominion embraces the heavens, earth, and everything between them; by wisdom He creates what He wills, gives daughters only or sons only, combines both, or makes people sterile.
rows.anchor: إناثا } فلا يولد له ذكر { ويهب لمن يشاء الذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ between nominative and accusative sawāʾ and between ghishāwah with or without alif; Abu Ali cautions that sawāʾ is a verbal noun, not an active participle that naturally modifies what precedes.
rows.anchor: ليس الوجه في الآية نصب سواء على أن تجريه على ما قبله على حد قولك

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: If sawāʾ is accusative, it can be analyzed in several ways: as a second object, as a circumstantial predicate, or through the time-phrase as its governing context.
rows.anchor: فأما من قرأ سواء بالنصب فإن انتصابه يحتمل ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in their living and dying may refer only to the disbelievers, making sawāʾ a predicate: their worldly life and death are alike in evil and distance from God’s mercy.
rows.anchor: أنه ضمير الكفار دون الذين آمنوا فكان سواء على هذا القول مرتفعا بأنه خبر مبتدأ مقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the heavens and earth in truth and for human benefit through moral responsibility and the opportunity for great reward; every soul is repaid for its deeds without loss of rights.
rows.anchor: وإنما خلقهما لنفع خلقه بأن يكلفهم ويعرضهم للثواب الجزيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Hasan, and Qatada say the person makes whatever he desires into his religion, following desire without fear or restraint.
rows.anchor: اتخذ دينه ما يهواه فلا يهوى شيئا إلا ركبه

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima and Saʿid ibn Jubayr say an idolater worships whichever stone or idol he finds more attractive, discarding the old one for it.
rows.anchor: وكان أحدهم يعبد الحجر فإذا رأى ما هو أحسن منه رمى به وعبد الآخر عن عكرمة وسعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Ali ibn Isa says the verse describes obeying desire as one obeys a deity, not believing that desire itself deserves worship.
rows.anchor: لم يرد أنه يعبد هواه ويعتقد أنه تحق له العبادة لأن ذلك لا يعتقده أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḍallah can mean God abandoned and left the person to his choice as just recompense for disbelief and refusal to reflect; another explanation is that God found him astray in accordance with prior knowledge.
rows.anchor: خذله الله وخلاه وما اختاره جزاء له على كفره وعناده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading takes aḍalla as losing or being separated from something, as in the poetic example of a man losing his camel.
rows.anchor: معناه أنه ضل عن الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God seals the person’s hearing and heart and covers his eyes; without God’s guidance, no one can guide someone who rejects clear guidance, so the warning calls listeners to take heed.
rows.anchor: وختم على سمعه وقلبه وجعل على بصره غشاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those denying resurrection say there is only worldly life, with no return or reckoning; their claim that time alone causes death reflects ignorance of the Creator and rests on conjecture.
rows.anchor: ليس الحياة إلا حياتنا التي نحن فيها في دار الدنيا ولا يكون بعد الموت بعث ولا حساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase we die and live may mean that the order is reversed, that people die and their children live, or that some die while others live.
rows.anchor: أن تقديره نحيا ونموت فقدم وأخر

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: If min is explanatory, all prophets are people of resolve because each accepted the mission and bore its burdens; most commentators and the apparent Imami reports instead take it partitively.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا القول فيكون جميع الأنبياء هم أولو العزم لأنهم عزموا على أداء الرسالة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The best-known view identifies five lawgiving messengers whose new law superseded the earlier one: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad; reports from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq call them the leading prophets.
rows.anchor: وهم خمسة أولهم نوح ثم إبراهيم ثم موسى ثم عيسى ثم محمد

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies six people of resolve by the trials they endured: Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph, and Job.
rows.anchor: هم ستة نوح صبر على أذى قومه وإبراهيم صبر على النار

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and al-Kalbi define them as those commanded to fight who openly confronted and struggled in religion; Abu al-Aliya instead names Abraham, Hud, Noah, and Muhammad.
rows.anchor: هم الذين أمروا بالجهاد والقتال وأظهروا المكاشفة وجاهدوا في الدين عن السدي والكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzm denotes obligation and firm resolve, and people of resolve are those who established laws and required people to follow them.
rows.anchor: والعزم هو الوجوب والحتم وأول العزم من الرسل هم الذين شرعوا الشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must not hurry their punishment, which is certain and near; when they see it, their long life in this world and the intermediate state will seem like one hour.
rows.anchor: إذا عاينوا العذاب صار طول لبثهم في الدنيا والبرزخ كأنه ساعة من نهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Balāgh may mean the Quran and its explanation as a communication from God, or may refer to that short duration as a sufficient announcement.
rows.anchor: بلاغ أي هذا القرآن وما فيه من البيان بلاغ من الله إليكم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The punishment befalls only the disobedient; Qatada further limits the destroyed to a polytheist who turned away from Islam or a hypocrite who affirmed with his tongue but acted otherwise.
rows.anchor: لا يهلك على الله تعالى إلا هالك مشرك ولى ظهره الإسلام أو منافق صدق بلسانه وخالف بعمله عن قتادة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says nothing offers stronger hope in God’s mercy than the assurance that only the wicked perish.
rows.anchor: وما جاء في الرجاء لرحمة الله شيء أقوى من هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise is brought close to those who avoid idolatry and sin, and it gathers every pleasure: rivers, trees, fine fruits, noble spouses, heavenly companions, servants, and ornate palaces.
rows.anchor: قربت الجنة وأدنيت للذين اتقوا الشرك والمعاصي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The garden is not far away; alternatively, its arrival is near because everything that is coming is near, as Hasan says.
rows.anchor: معناه ليس ببعيد مجيء ذلك لأن كل آت قريب

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Awwāb means someone who repeatedly repents and returns to obedience, according to al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd; Ibn Abbas and Ata instead gloss it as one who glorifies God.
rows.anchor: أي تواب رجاع إلى الطاعة عن الضحاك وابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥafīẓ describes someone who guards God’s commands and avoids forbidden acts, sins, and faults that would stain or diminish him.
rows.anchor: لما أمر الله به متحفظ من الخروج إلى ما لا يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing person believes in reward and punishment and obeys God without seeing Him; alternatively, fearing in the unseen means fearing Him in private, as al-Dahhak and al-Suddi say.
rows.anchor: أي هو من خاف الله وأطاعه وآمن بثوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person remains in this state until the afterlife, arriving with a heart turned back toward obedience and God.
rows.anchor: ودام على ذلك حتى وافى الآخرة بقلب مقبل على طاعة الله راجع إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entering Paradise in peace means security from harm and every affliction, or peace and greetings from God and His angels.
rows.anchor: ادخلوا الجنة بأمان من كل مكروه وسلامة من كل آفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Eternity is the lasting time in which the saved remain in bliss forever, without an end.
rows.anchor: الوقت الذي يبقون فيه في النعيم مؤبدين لا إلى غاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Paradise people receive whatever they desire, plus an increase beyond their wishes; another view says the increase exceeds the reward they earned by their deeds.
rows.anchor: وعندنا زيادة على ما يشاؤونه مما لم يخطر ببالهم ولم تبلغهم أمانيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many earlier generations who denied their messengers were destroyed despite being stronger and better equipped than Meccan unbelievers, so strength did not protect them.
rows.anchor: الذين أهلكناهم كانوا أشد قوة من هؤلاء وأكثر عدة وعدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naqqabū may mean that their strength opened roads throughout the land, or that they traveled and explored every route over long lives; none found a refuge from death.
rows.anchor: ساروا في البلاد وطوفوا فيها بقوتهم وسلكوا كل طريق
